criteria.label: Solar illumination
criteria.unit: fraction of year with Sun above local horizon
criteria.description: Fraction of the 12-month planning window in which the Sun is above the local terrain horizon modelled from LOLA. Values near 0.5 indicate a normal day/night cycle; polar peaks can exceed 0.8. Terrain shadowing is modelled only to a 5 km radius.
criteria.caveat: Upper-bound where terrain beyond 5 km or unresolved at 30-118 m blocks low Sun.

criteria.label: Direct-to-Earth link
criteria.unit: fraction of year with Earth >5° above local horizon
criteria.description: Fraction of the year with the Earth at least 5° above the terrain horizon, a conservative proxy for a usable direct-to-Earth radio link. Far-side sites score zero and require a relay.
criteria.caveat: A real link also needs a ground station, clear aperture, and link budget; 5° is a screening threshold, not a link-budget result.

criteria.label: Terrain trafficability
criteria.description: DEM-derived slope and residual roughness near the site. Lower slope and roughness are better. Uses the best available NASA Moon Trek DEM for each site (2-118 m/px), not a landed-vehicle-scale DTM.
criteria.caveat: Coarse compared with a lander footprint; boulders and metre-scale hazards are unresolved.

criteria.label: ISRU / water-ice access
criteria.unit: approx. distance to nearest mapped PSR edge (km)
criteria.description: Proximity to a mapped permanently shadowed region (PSR), used as a screening proxy for access to cold-trapped volatiles. The PSR layer is a centroid-and-area catalogue, so edge distance is approximate. Non-polar sites fall back to a documented analyst score.
criteria.caveat: PSR proximity is not proof of ice. LEND hydrogen, Mini-RF CPR, and Diviner temperature data are still required.

criteria.label: Science value
criteria.description: Relative scientific return of the site for a first crewed campaign: uniquely preserved material, process diversity, ground truth, and sample context.
criteria.caveat: Analyst judgment, not a measured quantity; the ranking sensitivity report shows how much it matters.

criteria.label: Thermal environment
criteria.description: Screening assessment of the thermal environment for crews and equipment: stable polar temperatures versus the 14-day equatorial day/night swing, and proximity to cryogenic PSRs.
criteria.caveat: No Diviner temperature time series was ingested; this is a qualitative screen.

criteria.label: Crew safety / operations
criteria.description: Non-slope operational hazards: cliffs, rilles, boulder fields, navigation in shadow, abort paths, and communications blackouts. Slope itself is scored separately under terrain.
criteria.caveat: Qualitative; requires a site-specific hazard map and LROC NAC imagery.

criteria.label: Data maturity / ground truth
criteria.description: How well the site is already mapped and, where applicable, ground-truthed. Higher scores mean lower mapping risk and better algorithm validation.
criteria.caveat: A high score means more existing data, not a better mission site.
